thread:
Maya (oncall): incident-bot just paged me for elevated 5xx rate on /v1/generate in us-west-2. seeing errors + console shows models healthy. starting triage. anyone on-call for controlplane?
incident-bot: PAGE -> @Maya (oncall) severity:high customers_impacted:some - alert_id:ALRT-1787 - src:dataplane-proxy
Maya (oncall): quick context: customer reports latency spikes and some calls returning 500/502. console metrics (frontend) show no config changes. traces show requests reaching control plane but dataplane returning errs. adding logs.
Sanjay: i'm on deck for control plane. linking logs I pulled from the API gateway: `curl -sS https://logs.internal/1787/api-gw | tail -n 120` -> `upstream reset before headers`, a bunch of `502 upstream reset` at 12:03:14-12:07:02 UTC.
Eli: i can take dataplane. i'm sshing into instance pool to check qps and kernel logs. quick check: pods show high `GRPC: -14 UNAVAILABLE` spikes. wonder if KV cache invalidations caused cold misses.
Tess: support thread from Avery says two enterprise customers got 500s for ~2m starting 12:03. They're asking for ETA/mitigation. Avery, can you paste exact customer error samples?
Avery (support): copying paste from customer1: `{"error":"server error","request_id":"c5b3"}` and from customer2: `502 bad gateway - runtime panic` (they included a stack snippet). both around 12:04. PRIO: high.
Maya (oncall): mitigation idea: route traffic to fallback model variant in us-west-2 and failover to dedicated pool in us-east-1 for affected customers. Can platform do on-the-fly routing policy change?
Ops-CLI: `rollout set-policy --region us-west-2 --route /v1/generate --fallback-model redwood-lite-v1 --dry-run=false` -> executed by Maya at 1787654385.
incident-bot: ACTION logged: routing policy change executed by Maya (oncall) at 1787654385.
Sanjay: hypothesis A: control plane config push failed for recent KV-rollout at 12:00, so dataplane nodes had partial config mismatch and rejected some requests. Evidence: controlplane logs show `config_push: ack timeout` around 12:01-12:02.
Eli: hypothesis B: dataplane autoscaler scaled down an isolated subset at 12:02 due to spurious metric anomaly and some requests hit cold nodes causing runtime errors. Evidence: `kube events` show `ScaledDown` for pool-3 at 12:02. attaching snippet: ```
12:02:01 kubelet pool-3 scaledown initiated
12:02:05 pool-3 terminated pod-18
12:03:10 pod-18 was still in terminating state when request arrived
```
Tess: also seeing console/api discrepancy: console shows model status = healthy for all models, but API head logs show `model not ready` for a small subset. possible stale cache in console or race in healthcheck aggregation.
Maya (oncall): can we build in-thread timeline for RCA? I'll drop a compact timeline and we can fill gaps.
Maya (oncall): TIMELINE DRAFT:
- 11:58 UTC: KV rollout initiated (control plane)
- 12:00 UTC: config push to dataplane starts
- 12:01-12:02 UTC: controlplane logs show `push: ack timeout` (some nodes unacked)
- 12:02 UTC: autoscaler scales down pool-3 (one node terminated)
- 12:03-12:06 UTC: spike in 502/5xx from dataplane; customers experience errors
- 12:06 UTC: routing policy change applied to fallback model in us-west-2 by oncall
- 12:10 UTC: errors subside, fallback routing mitigates error

Sanjay: adding logs to timeline: controlplane `push` trace id `trace-72a` shows repeated `grpc: deadline exceeded` to node pool-3 (ip 10.3.44.21). attaching minimal trace lines: `push/trace-72a: send->10.3.44.21: deadline exceeded`
Eli: dataplane node logs (10.3.44.21) show `oom_kill?` no; show `runtime panic: cache miss null ref` around 12:03:08; also `grpc: connection reset by peer` following.
Tess: note for RCA: console health aggregator polls a subset of endpoints (controlplane admin) not the per-node readiness. it reports healthy if admin responds, even if model worker is failing. this explains discrepancy.
Avery (support): customer impact summary for postmortem: two enterprise customers had degraded requests for ~3 minutes, no data loss, high error rate for specific routes. support classification: Sev2.
Maya (oncall): actions logged so far: routing-fallback applied, oncall notified SRE, controlplane attempted re-push to unacked nodes (manual retry at 12:08).
Sanjay: next steps for RCA collection: 1) stash full controlplane push logs for trace-72a 2) correlate autoscaler events with pod termination window 3) capture heap/profile of node 10.3.44.21 if possible (Eli?)
Eli: collecting `journalctl -u dataplane-worker -o short-precise --since \"2026-03-12 11:50\" > /tmp/dp-10.3.44.21.log` and `gcore` not available on prod nodes; will snapshot container logs and mem usage.
Tess: also flagging that console should show per-node worker readiness in the UI; raising product ticket after RCA.
Maya (oncall): hypothesis ranking: 1) controlplane push ack timeout + partial config mismatch (most likely) 2) autoscaler race causing terminating pods to receive traffic (possible contributing) 3) unrelated runtime bug triggered by cold-cache on one node (less likely).
Sanjay: agree. for in-thread hypothesis tracking: tagging hypotheses -> H1:push-ack-mismatch, H2:scaler-race, H3:cold-bug. We'll keep updates here.
Eli: initial artifact uploads: S3 links -> `s3://redwood-incident/1787654321/controlplane-push.log`, `s3://redwood-incident/1787654321/dp-10.3.44.21.log` (ACL internal).
incident-bot: NOTE: recorded mitigation `fallback-routing` and cleared pager at 1787654412 by Maya.
Avery (support): customers notified with post-incident note and workaround (switch to dedicated pool) while we finish RCA.
Maya (oncall): closing loop for now: mitigation held, customers stable, continuing RCA evidence collection. i'll own the RCA doc and link here when ready. tagging next oncall for followup: @Sanjay. :thumbsup:
Sanjay: ack. I'll pull full controlplane traces and work with infra to see if we can prevent push ack timeouts (networking/firewall flakiness).
Eli: I'll attach dataplane metrics and pod lifecycle graphs to the RCA.
Tess: filing product followup for console health visibility.
Maya (oncall): thanks all — keep updates short here, if fresh alerts happen re-page.
